blocks.text: View vs Edit — the real 1:1 test

content.value: Each component below is shown twice from the SAME real paper (composition-showcase): the published reader (VIEW, green) beside the live edit canvas (EDIT, amber). The edit side is the actual bp-paper-canvas mounting the real editor bundle — not a mock. Where the two halves differ, the promise of "edit is 1:1 with the reader" is not yet kept.

Left half of each image = VIEW (the reader). Right half = EDIT (the canvas). Scroll each pair: if the halves match, parity holds; if they differ, the verdict says what breaks. The task-list/fleet edit side is limited by this harness having no server to paint live rows — noted where it applies.
Paragraphs, headings, lists, and the two-column layout render essentially identically. Prose is the genuine 1:1 case.
Cells, header, and rules match. Fully editable AND visually identical.
Title bar, body command-lines, and footer match.
The card grid matches; edit adds faint input outlines (an acceptable edit affordance), not a layout change.

blocks.text: ✗ Where edit ≠ view — the real gaps
Section span/order — NOT applied in edit

content.value: VIEW: the callout spans two grid tracks (wide). EDIT: it collapses to one narrow column. Per-child span/order is paint-only — the layout you author is not shown while you edit it. This is a real node-view gap, not a harness artifact.

VIEW: a styled code frame + a rendered Mermaid diagram. EDIT: a raw textarea with a lang box, and the diagram shown as raw Mermaid SOURCE — no rendered preview. You edit source, you don't see the result.
VIEW packs label + lead + body into compact rows. EDIT stacks them vertically with extra spacing. Fully editable, but the shape differs from the reader — editable ≠ 1:1.
EDIT exposes the files/source fields as visible form chrome around the cell; VIEW is cleaner. Editable, but not visually identical.

blocks.text: Figure & Action — child not editable, extra chrome

content.value: Figure's caption is editable but its CHILD is a placeholder in edit (the actual content isn't authorable in-canvas). Action renders, but edit adds an href + priority row below the button.

VIEW shows the full live momentum board (bound rows). EDIT shows only a chip — because THIS harness has no server to paint the live rows. In real authenticated Studio the server would paint them, so this specific gap is likely a harness artifact, not a true divergence. Needs authenticated Studio to confirm.

Editability and visual parity are different axes. Prose, table, terminal, and cards are genuinely 1:1. Section-span, code, and diagram are real, fixable node-view gaps where edit shows form chrome or raw source instead of the rendered result. "Everything editable, 1:1 with the reader" is not yet true — this paper is the evidence, from a real paper, captured from the real editor bundle.
